# Data request checklist: more detailed paddy yield and its drivers

Send to: Department of Agriculture (Paddy Survey unit and state offices), KPKM statistics division, and the granary authority of the district
you want to study (for example MADA, KADA or IADA Kerian). Ask for 2010 to the latest season, in CSV or Excel.

## A. The yield itself (most important)
1. Yield (kg/ha), planted area (ha) and production (tonnes) for every season (main and off season), for the granary and, if possible, for each
   irrigation section / block / compartment.
2. The definition: all-season average or per season; moisture basis; how yield is calculated from the crop-cutting survey; how area is measured.
3. If crop-cutting plot data exist: plot or section id, location, sample size, date, yield.

## B. What may explain it (any that exist, per season and section)
4. Planting dates (start and finish of sowing) and the sowing method (wet, dry direct seeding, transplanting).
5. Variety planted and certified-seed use; date the certified seed arrived.
6. Water: days of irrigation supply, dam storage on key dates, any season where planting was delayed or water was short.
7. Pest and disease outbreaks: type, hectares affected, dates.
8. Floods and droughts that affected fields (dates, hectares).
9. Fertiliser and incentive schemes received (type, area covered).
10. Problem-soil area (for example acid sulphate) per section.

## How the project would use it
The extra yield records become the TARGET data (many more instances than seven yearly values). The other granaries, the DOSM 1980-2019
series and, if suitable, province-level rice statistics from similar countries become SOURCE data. The before-and-after test in the Model check
tab is then repeated, including instance weighting, which needs enough target instances to work.
